about: THE CHAIN mission_north (Design/content/CHAINS.md; the page is Design/content/chains/mission_north.md): carrying the mission north. Anskar sails for Birka with merchants in 829 and pirates take the emperor's gifts and nearly forty books on the way; King Bjorn lets him preach and the prefect Herigar builds a church on his own land; about 845 the people drive the priests out and Birka has none for nearly seven years; about 852 Anskar comes again, King Olaf asks the gods by lot and then the people at the thing, and an old man says that Christ has helped men at sea. Fourteen cards (thirteen harbour, one sea) in two acts a generation apart, each act with its own way in (829 at Sliesthorp or Dorestad; 830 at Birka; 845 at Birka; 850 and 852 at Sliesthorp). Four endings: ch_mission_north_end_church (what happened), ch_mission_north_end_endures (changed_birka_church_endures), ch_mission_north_end_merchants (changed_birka_merchants_church), ch_mission_north_end_refused (changed_birka_refused_mission); and one early change, changed_anskar_books_saved. Costs that last: ch_mission_north_bishop_watches, ch_mission_north_church_remembers. The spine's flag ms_carried_priest is set by step 9. Cast (Design/content/spine.json): cast.anskar, cast.herigar, cast.frideburg (all real, named in the words), cast.tidwine (invented). Real and named in the words but not in the spine's cast: Witmar, King Bjorn, King Olaf, the hermit Ardgar, the priest Erimbert, the exile Anound. Everything rests on Rimbert, Vita Anskarii c. 9-12, 14, 17-20, 25-28 (about 870; tr. C. H. Robinson 1921), given in our own plain rendering from memory of that translation, not re-read tonight (?). Every option's outcome text is a writing key named in its note. A draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start of act one: Sliesthorp or Dorestad, April to July 829. Anskar (cast.anskar, real, a monk of Corvey aged 27) and Witmar (real, his companion, a monk of the same house) want passage to Birka with the merchants. Sources: Rimbert c. 9 (envoys of the Svear ask the emperor Louis for priests; Anskar is chosen, Witmar goes with him), c. 10 (they travel with merchants, carrying the emperor's gifts and nearly forty books); chronicle_793.json 829-ansgar-birka. The port they sailed from is not recorded (?): Sliesthorp is the likeliest, and he passed Dorstadt in 826 (c. 7). That the chests went in the convoy's largest hull is invented, to fit a boat of 660 kg. Sets ch_mission_north_1, and _1_aboard if the monks are carried.

cards.title: Two monks and forty books
cards.intention: Two monks stand among the merchants who are making up a convoy for Birka. They have the emperor's gifts for the king of the Svear in sealed chests, and more books than most men here have seen in one place.

cards.note: Step 2: under way in 829 or 830 after step 1. The pirates. Sources: Rimbert c. 10: about half-way they fell among pirates; the merchants with them defended themselves hard and at first with success, were beaten in a second attack, and lost the ships and all they had; the monks barely got to land on foot; the emperor's gifts and nearly forty books were taken, and they kept only what they could carry as they left the ship; some wanted to turn back and Anskar would not. Who the pirates were and where is not recorded (?). The danger warns first: the sails are seen before the choice, and running costs only pride. Sets ch_mission_north_2 and either ch_mission_north_books_lost (and _chest if one chest is saved) or, if the fight is won, ch_mission_north_books_safe and changed_anskar_books_saved: history changed, the mission comes to Birka with the emperor's gifts and its books.

cards.note: Step 3: Birka, 829 or 830, after step 1. King Bjorn (real; Rimbert's Bern) hears the monks; Herigar (cast.herigar, real) is the king's prefect of the town. Sources: Rimbert c. 11: they came to Birka after a hard journey on foot and by ship over the waters between; the king received them kindly, took counsel with his friends and gave leave to stay and preach; many Christian captives were glad. Men of Birka had been to Dorstadt (c. 27). A gift for a king at table is how Anskar himself did it in 852 (c. 26); that a merchant gave one in 829 is invented. Sets ch_mission_north_3, and _3_wait for 200 days (the church is a winter's work).

cards.note: Step 4 (a side step): Ahus or Paviken, 829 to 836, once the books are lost. A dealer has what is left of them. Sources: the loss, Rimbert c. 10; the spine's thread book_road ('In 829 he sets out for Birka with nearly forty books and comes there on foot with none: someone has them'). What became of the books is not recorded: the card is invented. Raiders kept book fittings and threw away or sold the leaves: church metalwork cut from books lies in Norse graves (spine, holy_island), and the Canterbury Golden Gospels were bought back from a heathen army for gold (their own inscription, later 9th century). Ahus in Scania was a trading place in these years; that the pirates sold there is a guess (?). A book is 360 d in goods_793.json; these have no boards and have been wet. Sets ch_mission_north_4, and _books_bought, _books_sold or _4_told.

cards.note: Step 5, the end of act one and a second way in: Birka, 830 or 831, for any house (after the 200 days if it was at step 3). Herigar is baptised and has built a church on his own land; Anskar goes home after two winters with a letter from the king. Sources: Rimbert c. 11 (Herigar, 'a counsellor of the king', baptised, 'a little later built a church on his own ancestral property'; the Christian captives), c. 12 (they return after a year and a half with letters written by the king's own hand in the manner of the Svear, which is taken to mean runes (?)); chronicle_793.json 831-hamburg-see. Wine and wax for the Mass had to come by ship: wine is the lord's and the Mass's drink (BRIEF.md rule 2). The captive who reads is cast.tidwine (invented; a boy of Lindisfarne, 48 in 829: spine thread holy_island, hook at Birka). Every option carries Herigar's order for wine. Sets ch_mission_north_5; _5_books, _5_passage or _5_scribe.

cards.note: Step 6, the start of act two and a way in for any house: Birka, 845 to 850. The priests are gone. Sources: Rimbert c. 14 (Gautbert, consecrated bishop for the Svear, builds a church), c. 17 (about 845 the people rise, 'not by command of the king': they kill his nephew Nithard, bind the bishop and his companions and put them out of the land; no priest for nearly seven years), c. 19 (Herigar keeps the faith alone and argues at the thing; rain falls on the assembly and not on him and his boy), c. 20 (Frideburg, rich and old, bought wine and kept it in a vessel to be given her at her death in place of the sacrament); chronicle_793.json 845-hamburg-burned. Frideburg is cast.frideburg (real). That she bought the wine of this house is invented. Sets ch_mission_north_6, _6_wait for 60 days; _6_wine or _6_word.

cards.note: Step 7: Birka, 845 to 851, sixty days or more after step 6. The book on the fence. Sources: Rimbert c. 18: after the bishop was driven out, a man whose son had brought home a book from the plunder lost wife, son and daughter and most of his goods; a soothsayer he asked found every god content with him but Christ, who was against him because something hallowed to Christ was in his house; he remembered the book, bound it to a fence with word that whoever wished might take it, and a Christian carried it home. Rimbert had it from that Christian. Here the house can be that man. The farmer's words are invented. Sets ch_mission_north_7, _7_wait for 90 days; _7_book or _7_sold.

cards.note: Step 8: Birka, 846 to 850, ninety days or more after step 7. Anound's ships. Sources: Rimbert c. 19: Anound, a king of the Svear driven out, came against Birka with twenty-one ships of the Danes and eleven of his own; the king was far off, the people fled to the fort near by, and Herigar with the merchants and people who remained bought peace for a hundred pounds of silver; the Danes thought it too little; Herigar told the townsmen to stop offering to their gods and vow to Christ; lots were cast, the Danes found that their gods would not have the place sacked, and a further lot sent them against a town of the Slavs far off; Anound afterwards gave back what he had taken (?). The year lies between 845 and 851 (realms/sweden_gotland.md). The danger warns first: the fleet lies in the sound and asks a price. A hundred pounds is 24,000 d; a visiting boat's share of 60 d is invented. Sets ch_mission_north_8; _8_paid, _8_stood or _8_slipped.

cards.note: Step 9 and a way in for any house: Sliesthorp, 850 or 851. Anskar, now archbishop (Hamburg 831, burned 845; Bremen from 848), has a church by the harbour here by King Horik's leave and sends the hermit Ardgar to Birka. Sources: Rimbert c. 19-20 (Ardgar the anchorite sent to Birka about 851; Herigar receives the sacrament from him and dies; Frideburg dies; Ardgar goes home), c. 24 (the church at Sliaswic; merchants of Dorstadt and of this place come freely); chronicle_793.json 850-hedeby-church. That a Frisian hull carried Ardgar is invented. If the books bought at step 4 are still aboard (step 5 missed), he asks that they go on to Birka: they count on the hard road either way. Sets ch_mission_north_9; _9_carried and the spine's flag ms_carried_priest if he is carried.

cards.note: Step 10, the road to the finale and a way in for any house: Sliesthorp, April to August 852 or 853. Anskar goes to Birka himself. Sources: Rimbert c. 25-26: Bishop Gautbert will not go back and sends his nephew Erimbert, a priest; King Horik sends his own man and his token with Anskar to King Olaf, saying he has never known so good a man; the voyage takes nearly twenty days; Herigar died about 851 (c. 19). The year is 'about 852' (realms/sweden_gotland.md; one or two years either way (?)). A bell in a church was a thing 'the pagans regarded as unlawful' at Sliaswic (c. 32, of the later 850s): that one was carried to Birka is invented, and is what the hard road needs. Sets ch_mission_north_10, _10_wait for 15 days; ch_mission_north_bell.

cards.note: Step 11: Birka, 852 to 854, fifteen days or more after step 10. The town is uneasy and the king gives his answer. Sources: Rimbert c. 26: a man had come saying he had been at a meeting of the gods, who sent word that they had long been good to the Svear and were now given fewer offerings, and that if the people wanted more gods they would take the dead King Eric into their number; Anskar's friends told him to give up or to buy his life with what he had; he asked the king to a meal, gave gifts and showed Horik's token; King Olaf answered that priests had been driven out before by a rising of the people and not by a king's command, so he would ask the gods by lot and then the people at the thing, 'It is our custom that the control of public business of every kind should rest with the whole people and not with the king' (tr. Robinson 1921, as quoted in spine.json). The chief who asks the house which way it will speak is invented. Sets ch_mission_north_11, _11_wait for 3 days; _11_mission, _11_old or _11_house.

cards.note: Step 12: Birka, three days or more after step 11. The lot. Sources: Rimbert c. 27: the king first met his chiefs; they chose to ask by lot, went out into the open field as their custom was, and the lot fell that it was the will of God that the Christian worship be set up there. How the Svear cast is not told: the marked slips on a white cloth are Tacitus, Germania 10, seven centuries older and of other peoples (?). The lot is the one true chance in the story, so it is a chance here: likely, as the word goes. Paying the man who throws is invented; that lots could be doubted is not (c. 19: the Danes cast again and again). A lot against moves the story to step 14, not to its end. Sets ch_mission_north_12, _12_wait for 2 days, and _lot_for or _lot_against; _lot_bought.

cards.note: Step 13, the finale when the lot fell for it: Birka, two days or more after step 12. The thing. Sources: Rimbert c. 27: the matter was cried at the assembly at Birka, there was uproar, and an old man rose and said that many of them knew this god helps those who hope in him, in peril at sea and other straits; that some who had been to Dorstadt had taken up this worship of their own will; that the way there was now beset by pirates; and why should they not take at home what they had sought far off. The people agreed; a second assembly in another part of the realm agreed also. c. 28: the king gave a hall to be an oratory and Anskar bought another plot for the priest's house; Erimbert stayed. Endings: ch_mission_north_end_church (what happened); ch_mission_north_end_endures with changed_birka_church_endures (the hard road: the bell, a book brought back, and a priest carried or Herigar stood by); ch_mission_north_end_merchants with changed_birka_merchants_church (the church is the house's own, as Herigar's was his: the proprietary church of the age) and the cost ch_mission_north_bishop_watches; ch_mission_north_end_refused with changed_birka_refused_mission and the cost ch_mission_north_church_remembers. All set ch_mission_north_done.

cards.note: Step 14, the finale when the lot fell against: Birka, two days or more after step 12. This did not happen: in Rimbert c. 27 the lot fell for the mission. Here the king cannot put a thing to the people that the gods have refused, and the story goes on by another road: the archbishop is carried home (ending refused, with the archbishop's protection: a free man under a bishop's hand, as in unlocks_793.json unlock_title_lords_protection); or a smaller question is put to the lot, whether strangers may keep their own god on their own plot (ending merchants), which is how Herigar's church stood, on a man's own land (c. 11); or the old man is brought before the chiefs all the same (ending church); or the old party thanks the house (ending refused, their way). A failed chance pays the loyal ending, never nothing. The same four ending flags and costs as step 13.
